item.title: Update: Linux TCP use-after-free: Citrix XenServer and XCP-ng fixes are out, WatchGuard and Fortinet still have none
item.description: Citrix rates its XenServer bulletin Critical (XenServer 8.4 and 9, Workload Balancing and Conversion Manager affected, fixes named), XCP-ng released a kernel fix, MikroTik's RouterOS 7.25.1 and 7.24.6 list the CVE, and WatchGuard lists Fireware OS, AP and Dimension as potentially affected with no fix; Vates, XCP-ng and WatchGuard say a public exploit exists or circulates, which the MPTCP exploit being unable to run on XCP-ng and Fireware OS tempers, and no source reports attacks.
item.content:encoded:
Update05 Nov 2026 04:04 UTCrun 2026-11-05T0255Z-inteltitleheadlinesummaryentitiesaffected_productscvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

Citrix rates its XenServer bulletin Critical (XenServer 8.4 and 9, Workload Balancing and Conversion Manager affected, fixes named), XCP-ng released a kernel fix, MikroTik's RouterOS 7.25.1 and 7.24.6 list the CVE, and WatchGuard lists Fireware OS, AP and Dimension as potentially affected with no fix; Vates, XCP-ng and WatchGuard say a public exploit exists or circulates, which the MPTCP exploit being unable to run on XCP-ng and Fireware OS tempers, and no source reports attacks.

Citrix's bulletin CTX697256 of 2026-11-03, rated Critical, says an unauthenticated attacker on the management network may compromise a XenServer host and any running Workload Balancing or Conversion Manager appliance; it affects XenServer 8.4 and 9, Workload Balancing before 2026.1.1 and Conversion Manager before 2026.2.0, and Citrix has pushed updates to the Early Access and Normal channels of each XenServer line without naming a build and released Workload Balancing 2026.1.1 or later and Conversion Manager 2026.2.0 (Citrix, 2026-11-03). The bulletin states no exploitation.

Vates's advisory VSA-2026-056, published on 2026-11-03 and updated on 2026-11-04, rates the flaw critical for XCP-ng 8.3 and the Xen Orchestra Appliance, lists the fixed packages kernel-4.19.19-8.0.46.14.xcpng8.3 and, for the appliance, linux 6.1.190-1, requires a reboot, and gives an interim mitigation that drops inbound IP options, because without IP options the vulnerable code path cannot be reached (Vates, 2026-11-04). XCP-ng's post of 2026-11-04 says anyone who can send TCP traffic to the host, for example from its management network, VMs on it included, can attempt the attack, and tells hosts that cannot reboot at once to apply the iptables-based mitigation and not yet the update (XCP-ng, 2026-11-04). XCP-ng says a public exploit exists that relies on MPTCP, which the XCP-ng 8.3 kernel does not have, so it does not work against XCP-ng, while the underlying bug is present and other ways to exploit it cannot be ruled out (XCP-ng, 2026-11-04); Vates says the exploit does not affect XCP-ng and the bug is not specific to MPTCP (Vates, 2026-11-04).

WatchGuard's advisory WGSA-2026-0033 of 2026-11-03 lists Fireware OS, AP and Dimension as potentially affected with no fix, says Fireware OS and AP do not enable MPTCP and are not affected by the exploit chain circulating online, and says it will update the advisory when Ubuntu ships a fix for Dimension (WatchGuard, 2026-11-03). MikroTik's RouterOS 7.25.1 of 2026-11-02 and RouterOS 7.24.6 of 2026-10-30 list the CVE under "improve stability" (MikroTik, 2026-11-02; MikroTik, 2026-10-30). NCSC Switzerland's advisory 13120 of 2026-10-29 rates exploitation unknown with vendor patches available and names MPTCP listeners as the target of the known exploits (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-10-29). Fortinet's advisory is unchanged: still investigating, with no fixed build, and Known Exploited: No (Fortinet, 2026-11-02).

Open finding: CVE-2026-98432, Linux kernel IPv4 TCP: a use-after-free in connection setup, present since 4.4, has an Anthropic-built remote root exploit against MPTCP listeners that CloudLinux could not reproduce; Citrix XenServer, XCP-ng, MikroTik, Red Hat, Debian, CIQ and Amazon Linux have fixes, Ubuntu's are in progress and WatchGuard and Fortinet have none for their products (CVSS 9.8) →

item.title: Update: Refrigeration attacks reach Switzerland, a Köniz butcher and three Volg stores; no actor established
item.description: The French blood service EFS confirmed that an incident at its refrigeration supplier on 2 November altered the temperature and defrost thresholds of cold rooms at three of its sites, caught by its own alarms with no loss of blood products, so the case no longer rests on Le Canard enchaîné alone; ENISA, the European Commission, Europol and the CSIRTs Network advised organisations on 2026-11-04 to take immediate action, CSIRT Italia issued cold-chain measures, and no source ties the blood-service case to the Danfoss, Copeland or Dixell controllers.
item.content:encoded:
Update05 Nov 2026 04:02 UTCrun 2026-11-05T0255Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarysectorssourcesevidencesourcing_notebody

The French blood service EFS confirmed that an incident at its refrigeration supplier on 2 November altered the temperature and defrost thresholds of cold rooms at three of its sites, caught by its own alarms with no loss of blood products, so the case no longer rests on Le Canard enchaîné alone; ENISA, the European Commission, Europol and the CSIRTs Network advised organisations on 2026-11-04 to take immediate action, CSIRT Italia issued cold-chain measures, and no source ties the blood-service case to the Danfoss, Copeland or Dixell controllers.

The French blood service EFS confirmed on 2026-11-03 that on 2 November a refrigeration-equipment supplier suffered a cybersecurity incident that affected the supervision and control installations of cold rooms at three EFS sites, with temperature and defrost thresholds raised to very high values (translated from French) (EFS, 2026-11-03). EFS says its own monitoring and alarm systems identified the anomalies quickly, the affected equipment was brought under control without impact on the products or neutralised, the products stored in those cold rooms were transferred preventively to other installations, and no health impact or loss of blood products is to be reported; it names no supplier and gives no temperature figure (translated from French) (EFS, 2026-11-03).

BleepingComputer, heise and SRF identify the supplier as Coolworld, and SRF reports that the attackers reportedly entered through its remote maintenance (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-04; heise, 2026-11-04; SRF, 2026-11-04). Coolworld's statement of 2026-11-04 says the incident involved remote monitoring software, that the vulnerability reported in the media relates to a component from a third-party supplier outside its control and that a limited number of its units were affected; it does not say that attackers exploited that component (Coolworld, 2026-11-04). BleepingComputer's account reads it the other way, saying Coolworld says the attackers exploited a vulnerability in a third-party component, which the statement does not state (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-04). No source names Danfoss, Copeland or Dixell equipment for this case.

ENISA, the European Commission (DG CNECT), Europol's EC3, the EU CSIRTs Network and EU-CyCLONe issued a joint statement on 2026-11-04: since 11 October 2026 several commercial refrigeration systems and similar devices have been hit in a number of EU Member States, a new wave occurred on 1 to 2 November, affected Member States are investigating and issuing guidance, and organisations are advised to take immediate action to mitigate exposure in the affected systems; it names no product, actor or count and does not mention Switzerland (ENISA, 2026-11-04). CSIRT Italia's bulletin of 2026-11-04 extends its call to every operator of cold-chain technology, whatever the sector, to apply its earlier measures urgently, removing direct internet exposure of administrative and control interfaces and verifying that operating parameters and alarms are intact first (CSIRT Italia, 2026-11-04). Its bulletin of 2026-10-13, re-issued on 2026-11-04 as version 1.2, asks operators to limit supplier access to authorised resources and periods, to require multi-factor authentication on remote access, applied on the mediating system when the device cannot do it, and to check actual temperatures and alarms with instruments independent of the supervision platform (CSIRT Italia, 2026-11-04). The BSI had urged operators of networked freezer controllers to disconnect them from the internet or at least secure and patch them (heise, 2026-11-04).

Open finding: Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controllers compromised, with forced defrost at hundreds of French supermarkets, refrigeration failures at more than 115 shops in at least six more countries and first cases in Germany, and on 2026-11-02 altered settings in the cold rooms of the French blood service through a refrigeration supplier, and on 2026-11-05 the first publicly known cases in Switzerland; responsibility not established; ENISA and Europol call for immediate action →

item.title: Update: Zyxel GS1900: Binarly says the exploit GreyNoise caught works on the June-fixed builds; install the .3C0 builds

item.content:encoded:

item.title: SonicWall GMS 9.5.2 and earlier: unauthenticated file read, no fix will ship; replace with NSM
item.description: SonicWall's advisory SNWLID-2026-0019 of 2026-11-03 says an unauthenticated attacker with network access to SonicWall GMS 9.5.2 and earlier may read internal GMS files (CVE-2026-109593, CVSS 3.1 9.1), with a post-authentication SQL injection beside it (CVE-2026-109594, 6.8). ROUTINECVE-2026-109593 +1NATOA2

CVE-2026-109593 and CVE-2026-109594, SonicWall GMS 9.5.2 and earlier: an unauthenticated network attacker may read internal GMS files (CVSS 3.1 9.1), and SonicWall says the end-of-life product gets no fix and has no workaround

SonicWall's advisory SNWLID-2026-0019 of 2026-11-03 covers the end-of-life Global Management System: an unauthenticated attacker with network access to GMS 9.5.2 and earlier may be able to read internal GMS files, potentially exposing sensitive information (CVE-2026-109593, CVSS 3.1 9.1), and a post-authentication SQL injection under specific conditions could let an authenticated attacker access or modify data (CVE-2026-109594, 6.8) (SonicWall, 2026-11-03). The advisory lists no workaround and no fixed version, says no remediation or security update will be released because the product has reached end of life, and strongly encourages migration to Network Security Manager (SonicWall, 2026-11-03). End of support was 2026-09-30 (SonicWall, 2025-05-05), and the previous GMS advisory of 2026-08-11 named 9.5.2 as the fixed build for its flaws, so the last fixed build is itself affected now (SonicWall, 2026-08-11). The advisory does not say which files are exposed or whether anyone exploits the flaw, and CERT-FR relays it (CERT-FR, 2026-11-04).

Exposure
A GMS Virtual Appliance or Windows installation on 9.5.2 or earlier that is reachable from a network the operator does not trust; every such installation is unpatchable (SonicWall, 2026-11-03).
Defender takeaway
With no fix and no workaround the levers are reachability and replacement: take any GMS instance off untrusted networks and migrate to Network Security Manager, as SonicWall urges (SonicWall, 2026-11-03).

item.title: APT29-linked watering hole uses n-day iOS and Chrome chains; CISA lists CVE-2024-27834; updated devices resist
item.description: Sekoia reports a watering-hole campaign it assesses with moderate to high confidence to be APT29 or a subgroup, serving platform-specific exploit chains for iOS 16.7, a DarkSword-based iOS chain and Chrome 139 to 145 on Android through injected sites, clone domains and a one-week compromise of the Plerdy analytics script; Sekoia says none of the chains works against fully updated devices. CISA added the Apple WebKit pointer-authentication bypass CVE-2024-27834, the second step of the iOS 16.7 chain and fixed in May 2024, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-04; no Swiss victim is named.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLECVE-2024-27834 +7exploitedNATOB2

Sekoia: an APT29-linked watering hole serves n-day iOS and Android exploit chains through compromised sites, clone domains and a one-week compromise of the Plerdy tracker; CISA lists the Apple WebKit pointer-authentication bypass CVE-2024-27834 as exploited on 2026-11-04

CISA added CVE-2024-27834, a WebKit flaw that lets an attacker with arbitrary read and write capability bypass Pointer Authentication and that Apple fixed on 2024-05-13, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-04, and names no victim or method (CISA KEV, 2026-11-04; Apple, 2024-05-13; Apple, 2024-05-13). The same day Sekoia reported a watering-hole campaign that it assesses with moderate to high confidence to be APT29 or one of its subgroups and in which that flaw is the pointer-authentication bypass of an iOS chain (Sekoia, 2026-11-04); the link between the listing and the campaign is the date alone. Sekoia retrieved three chains from the delivery host, which profiles the visitor and serves a platform-specific exploit without user interaction: an iOS 16.7 chain (CVE-2025-43529, then CVE-2024-27834) that steals the cookies of running apps; a DarkSword-based iOS chain that Sekoia's table labels iOS 18.5 (CVE-2025-43529 with CVE-2026-20700, then CVE-2025-14174 with CVE-2025-43510, then CVE-2025-43520) that harvests the phone; and an Android chain for Chrome 139 to 145 except 143 (CVE-2026-3910, then the Adreno driver flaw CVE-2025-27038) that takes Chrome cookies, saved logins, history and Wi-Fi configuration (Sekoia, 2026-11-04). The payloads exfiltrate data without establishing persistence, and Sekoia says none of the chains contains a zero-day or works against fully updated devices (Sekoia, 2026-11-04).

Delivery used JavaScript injected into legitimate sites, among them a Ukrainian gas producer, a US chemical-industry trade association, a Bulgarian military-related site and an Australian clinic; reverse-proxy clones of high-profile sites; and a one-week compromise, 27 August to 3 September 2026, of the Plerdy SEO tracker script, which Sekoia says exposed hundreds or thousands of sites, mostly Ukrainian (Sekoia, 2026-11-04). Sekoia names no Swiss victim, counts no infected devices and says it is working with national CERTs on victim identification.

Exposure
IPhones and iPads below the builds that fix the six iOS flaws, and Android phones on Chrome before the fix of CVE-2026-3910 or an unpatched Adreno driver. Sekoia's iOS 16.7 chain filters for iOS 16.7 and 16.7.10, and the sources do not establish whether the later 16.7.x builds Apple lists for iPhone 8, 8 Plus, X, iPad 5th generation and the first-generation iPad Pro models, up to 16.7.16 of 2026-05-11, are exploitable (Sekoia, 2026-11-04; Apple, 2026-05-11).

Fixes: iOS 26.2 and 18.7.3 close CVE-2025-43529 and CVE-2025-14174, iOS 26.1 and 18.7.2 close CVE-2025-43510 and CVE-2025-43520, iOS 26.3 closes CVE-2026-20700, and Chrome 146 closes CVE-2026-3910 (Apple, 2025-12-12; Google Threat Intelligence Group, 2026-03-18; Chrome Releases, 2026-03-12).

Detection
Sekoia names one on-device trace, a marker cookie that the iOS 16.7 chain's script sets as a replay guard so the exploit does not fire twice on a victim; it publishes some indicators and withholds several delivery and exfiltration hosts, so a visit to an injected site shows in web proxy and DNS telemetry from managed phones only against indicators obtained from Sekoia or a national CERT; the dependable check is the OS and Chrome version inventory (Sekoia, 2026-11-04).
Defender takeaway
Bring managed iOS devices to the newest release for each model and Android phones to current Chrome and the OEM patch level, because Sekoia says updated devices resist these chains and CISA lists every flaw they deliver as exploited (Sekoia, 2026-11-04; CISA KEV, 2026-11-04); the devices that cannot go past iOS 16.7.x are the open question.

item.title: SEPPmail gateway: unauthenticated sender reaches root RCE or file access; fixed in 15.1.1, 15.0.x has no fix
item.description: SEPPmail's patch release 15.1.1 of 2026-11-03 fixes five flaws in the Secure Email Gateway, with NCSC.ch as the CNA: CVE-2026-114424 lets an unauthenticated remote sender run operating-system commands as root through an active address-replacement rule that uses message-derived data, and CVE-2026-114425 lets one disclose, move or delete files as root when Large File Transfer is enabled (both CVSS 4.0 9.2). The vendor says 15.0.7 was the last 15.0 release, so 15.0.x gateways must move to the 15.1 branch; no source reports exploitation.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLECVE-2026-114424 +4NATOA2

CVE-2026-114424 and CVE-2026-114425, SEPPmail Secure Email Gateway before 15.1.1: an unauthenticated mail sender can reach root command execution through a replacement rule and root file access through Large File Transfer, with three more flaws fixed in the same release and no fix for the 15.0 branch (CVSS 4.0 9.2)

SEPPmail's revision history lists patch release 15.1.1 of 2026-11-03 with five security fixes in the Secure Email Gateway, all for versions before 15.1.1 (SEPPmail, 2026-11-03). Two are unauthenticated and rated 9.2: in CVE-2026-114424 attacker-influenced replacement text in sender or recipient address-replacement rules is evaluated as Perl code, so a remote sender can run operating-system commands in the mail-processing worker when an active rule uses message-derived replacement data and its search condition matches, and the validated worker context was root (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-04); in CVE-2026-114425 a file path supplied in the attachment metadata of an incoming message lets the worker disclose, move or delete an accessible file when Large File Transfer is enabled, also as root (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-04). CVE-2026-114426 lets an unauthenticated attacker exhaust workers and disk because the upload interface processed data before checking authentication (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-04), and two flaws in the GINA webmail let an unauthenticated attacker take over a created but unregistered account with an empty initial password (CVE-2026-114421) and enumerate email addresses through an unescaped LDAP filter (CVE-2026-114420) (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-04; ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-04). The vendor says 15.0.7 of 2026-09-02 is the last release of the 15.0 branch, so the fix for a 15.0.x gateway is the move to 15.1 (SEPPmail, 2026-11-03). None of the sources read reports exploitation.

Exposure
A SEPPmail Secure Email Gateway before 15.1.1; the Home page of the administration interface shows the running version in the System section as "Firmware version" (SEPPmail, retrieved 2026-11-05). CVE-2026-114424 applies where an active rule uses message-derived replacement data, and CVE-2026-114425 where Large File Transfer is enabled (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-04; ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-04).
Detection
No source publishes an indicator. What the mechanism implies, not stated by a source: a child process or shell started by the mail-processing worker after inbound mail whose sender or recipient strings reach a replacement rule, and file operations by the Large File Transfer worker outside its storage area, both running as root.
Defender takeaway
Upgrade to 15.1.1, moving 15.0.x gateways to the 15.1 branch because 15.0 gets no fix, and until then review which active replacement rules use values taken from the message and whether Large File Transfer is enabled, the two conditions the CNA names (SEPPmail, 2026-11-03). Because the worker runs as root, a gateway that was exposed with such a rule or with Large File Transfer enabled warrants a compromise check.

item.title: Sophos RCA: fake interview repo ran BeaverTail via VS Code settings; dead EDR agent, OAuth grant survived revocation
item.description: Sophos discloses, as the victim, that on 2026-09-14 an employee cloned a repository presented as a job-interview coding assignment and opened it as a trusted VS Code workspace; its settings replaced the terminal profile, so opening a terminal downloaded and ran the BeaverTail loader and the in-memory InvisibleFerret backdoor on a Mac whose Sophos Endpoint agent had not reported since 2026-06-11. A third-party OAuth authorization on the employee's code-platform account survived the session revocation and read two internal repositories 27 times; Sophos found no other host and no customer impact.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB2

Sophos's own root-cause analysis of a developer-targeted intrusion: a fake job-interview repository's VS Code workspace settings ran BeaverTail and InvisibleFerret on a Mac whose endpoint agent had not reported since 11 June, and a third-party OAuth authorization outlived the session revocation

On 2026-09-14 a Sophos employee cloned a public repository presented as a job-interview coding assignment and opened it as a workspace in VS Code; a weaponized workspace settings file replaced the editor's integrated terminal profile with a command that downloads and runs a remote script in a loop, delivery relied on the user opening the workspace as trusted, and no exploit or vulnerability was involved (Sophos RCA, 2026-11-04). Opening a terminal was enough: a shell script fetched a JavaScript component and a package manifest into a hidden directory in the user profile, a package-manager install ran, the JavaScript ran under Node.js and the final-stage backdoor lived in memory only, with no persistence found (Sophos RCA, 2026-11-04). SophosLabs identified the BeaverTail loader followed by the InvisibleFerret backdoor, able to steal browser-stored credentials, keychain data and SSH keys, and the JavaScript stage sent the process environment to an attacker web endpoint on a cloud application-hosting service (Sophos RCA, 2026-11-04).

Two gaps lengthened the exposure. The Sophos Endpoint agent was installed but its core services were not running, so it enforced nothing and reported nothing; the device was last seen in Sophos Central on 2026-06-11, the cause is still under investigation, and SophosLabs says a working agent would have blocked the chain at the first dropped file (Sophos RCA, 2026-11-04). A third-party application authorization on the employee's source-code platform account survived the session revocation and password reset of 2026-09-15 and made 27 read requests against two internal repositories from an address new to the user until it was revoked on 2026-09-16; Sophos found no other host, no cloud activity and no customer impact (Sophos RCA, 2026-11-04). The analysis names no group; Sophos CTU says the technique matches the tradecraft of NICKEL ALLEY, which it describes as running the Contagious Interview campaign of fake companies, fake recruiters and malicious code repositories (Sophos blog, 2026-11-04).

Exposure
Developer workstations whose users clone and open repositories from outside parties, recruitment pretexts included, in an editor that trusts the workspace; and any managed device that is compliant in identity and device management but does not report to the endpoint console, as Sophos's fleet review found (Sophos RCA, 2026-11-04).
Detection
In macOS process lineage, the code editor's integrated terminal launching a download-and-run command that a cloned workspace's settings define, followed by a hidden directory in the user profile and a package-manager install run from it (Sophos RCA, 2026-11-04). In identity telemetry, a device that still signs in but does not report to the endpoint console is a coverage gap; a third-party authorization reading repositories from an address new to the user is the second signal (Sophos blog, 2026-11-04; Sophos RCA, 2026-11-04).

Triage: a terminal profile normally launches a shell executable; this one launched a command that downloads and runs a remote script in a loop; it came from the settings of a freshly cloned repository (Sophos RCA, 2026-11-04).

Defender takeaway
Treat a coding assignment or repository from a recruiter or interviewer as untrusted code, because here the compromise needed only a trusted workspace and an opened terminal. Sophos's lasting controls are to require the endpoint agent for device compliance, to monitor for managed devices that stop reporting, and to revoke application authorizations as part of credential containment, not only sessions and passwords (Sophos RCA, 2026-11-04).

Builds on: Binance's report: fake recruiter, trojaned pyenv, AI-tool pivot and a deployment token reached…

item.title: SpecterOps: iSCSI Target Server without CHAP lets a host that knows the target and initiator names read shared disks
item.description: SpecterOps (2026-11-04) shows that a Windows iSCSI Target Server configured as a common cluster guide describes, with the optional CHAP step skipped, accepts a login from any host that knows the target host, the target name and an authorised initiator name, and the post says the host and the names can be found. The attacker then reads the shared disk below file-system permissions; where it holds a Hyper-V domain controller's virtual disk, the directory database and local credential stores are exposed. CHAP, network segmentation and volume encryption are the levers.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB2

SpecterOps: a Windows iSCSI Target Server set up without CHAP lets any host that knows the target and an authorised initiator name read the shared disks below file permissions, a Hyper-V domain controller's among them

SpecterOps shows that the Windows iSCSI Target Server role, set up as a community cluster guide describes it with the optional CHAP step skipped, accepts a login from any host that knows the target host, the target name and an authorised initiator name (SpecterOps, 2026-11-04). The post says the role registers a service principal name on its computer account, so a directory query lists the target hosts, that initiator names are built from the host's DNS name and are therefore predictable, and that in the author's experience the service has no rate limiting or brute-force protection (SpecterOps, 2026-11-04). Access is below the file system, so NTFS permissions do not apply, and volume encryption such as BitLocker defeats it (SpecterOps, 2026-11-04). The worst case the post shows is a volume that holds a Hyper-V domain controller's virtual disk, from which the local credential stores and the directory database can be taken (SpecterOps, 2026-11-04). The author has not tested the technique in production and warns that it can cause outages, and the post cites no Microsoft response.

Exposure
Windows Server hosts that run the iSCSI Target Server role without CHAP, found by the service principal name the role registers and by a listener on TCP 3260 (SpecterOps, 2026-11-04; Pen Test Partners, 2016-05-18). The author's own research puts the common uses with clustered resources such as Hyper-V, SQL Server and Exchange database availability groups, followed by third-party backup products (SpecterOps, 2026-11-04).
Detection
The post names no telemetry. What the mechanism implies, not stated by the post: iSCSI traffic to TCP 3260 on a target host from a source that is not one of its cluster nodes, and a login that presents a listed initiator name from another source address, because the access list keys on initiator names that an impersonator can present (SpecterOps, 2026-11-04).
Defender takeaway
Enable CHAP on every iSCSI target, and isolate iSCSI traffic with segmentation and host-based firewalling, which the post calls arguably the most effective step; the post says IPsec mitigates network sniffing, and BitLocker or similar volume encryption makes the stolen disk unreadable (SpecterOps, 2026-11-04). Treat the disks of any domain controller that sat on an unprotected target as exposed.

item.title: Vaud: device-code phishing against Microsoft 365 is running in Romandie; several organisations already affected
item.description: The canton of Vaud said on 2026-11-04 that a Microsoft 365 device-code phishing campaign is running in French-speaking Switzerland and that several organisations are already affected: mail that appears to come from a company or a known contact leads the reader to type a code on a genuine Microsoft sign-in page, which gives the attacker access to the account. Microsoft documents a Conditional Access policy that blocks the device code flow for tenants that do not need it.
item.content:encoded:
HIGHNATOA2

Canton Vaud warns of a device-code phishing campaign against Microsoft 365 accounts running in French-speaking Switzerland, with several organisations already affected

The canton of Vaud said on 2026-11-04 that a phishing campaign is currently running in French-speaking Switzerland and that several organisations have already been affected (translated from French) (Canton of Vaud, 2026-11-04). The messages can appear to come from a company or a known contact and invite the reader to view an invoice, open a document or verify information through a link; the campaign uses device-code phishing, which gets the victim to type a code on a genuine Microsoft authentication page and so gives the attackers fraudulent access to the Microsoft 365 account (Canton of Vaud, 2026-11-04). The links printed in the notice combine a company-style name and a portal word on a workers.dev subdomain whose second label starts with a cloud-storage word and an identifier, and the canton says other addresses can be used too (Canton of Vaud, 2026-11-04); workers.dev is the route assigned to every Cloudflare Worker (Cloudflare Docs, 2026-09-22). The notice names no actor, kit, count of organisations, sector or start date.

Exposure
Any Microsoft 365 tenant whose users can complete the device code flow, which Microsoft describes as meant for devices without local input such as shared devices or digital signage and as a high-risk method that phishing can use (Microsoft Learn, 2026-03-24).
Detection
Mail, web proxy and DNS telemetry for links to workers.dev subdomains of the structure above; in the Entra sign-in logs, device code events found with the authentication protocol filter (Microsoft Learn, 2026-03-24). Microsoft says protocol tracking persists through token refreshes, so later sign-ins in the same session can fall under an authentication-flows policy, and it records an original transfer method property in the activity details of the Conditional Access sign-in logs (Microsoft Learn, 2026-03-24).

Triage: Microsoft documents device code sign-in for shared devices and signage; a device-code sign-in by a user who has no such device, soon after that user received a mailed link, falls outside that use (Microsoft Learn, 2026-03-24).

Defender takeaway
Where the tenant has no documented need for device code flow, Microsoft recommends blocking it with a Conditional Access policy, testing in report-only mode and auditing existing use first (Microsoft Learn, 2026-04-07). Tell users never to enter a Microsoft login code at a third party's request, and that anyone who has entered a code or validated an authentication request must call IT support at once, which is the canton's own instruction (Canton of Vaud, 2026-11-04).

Builds on: FBI PSA260521, Kali365 OAuth device-code PhaaS bypasses M365 MFA without credential capture · Huntress: stolen post-MFA M365 tokens replayed within minutes; a password reset leaves planted…

Xerox's bulletin of 2026-11-03 adds two interim measures for AltaLink, EC81xx, VersaLink and WorkCentre devices, restricting the web interface to trusted networks or management hosts or disabling HTTP/HTTPS, and says the vulnerable PHP component serves a limited number of pages of the embedded web server; fix dates are unchanged.

It says the vulnerable PHP component is used by a limited number of pages in the device's embedded web server, and that until the fix is installed customers can restrict the web interface (HTTP/HTTPS) to trusted networks or management hosts, for example with a firewall or segmentation, or disable HTTP/HTTPS if remote web administration is not required, which also disables the embedded web server and the features that depend on it (Xerox, 2026-11-03). The section does not cover the Fiery Digital Front End or the Worldwide Ticketing Tool, and the affected table and the fix dates are unchanged.

Open finding: CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, Xerox AltaLink, EC81xx, VersaLink and WorkCentre printers and Fiery print controllers: Xerox lists them as affected by the PHP2Shell flaws, with fixes expected on 2026-11-06 and Fiery patches between 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-23 →

item.title: Bitdefender: a 3AM affiliate joined a school estate's AD domains with new trusts after stealing Veeam credentials
item.description: Bitdefender MDR describes a September 2026 intrusion by a 3AM ransomware affiliate into a UK school estate that began as several unconnected Active Directory domains: a modified public Veeam script decrypted credentials stored on three backup servers, the attacker created two backdoor domain-administrator accounts, joined three domains with new two-way trusts within about three hours, tried to remove EDR agents (anti-tampering blocked it) and encrypted machines. Initial access is unknown, every attacker action Bitdefender saw came from an unmanaged internal host, and Bitdefender reads the 40 to 101 second retry cadence as a model-driven loop, flagged as its own interpretation; it says a new trust between domains is a rare change that is cheap to alert on.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB2

3AM ransomware affiliate in a UK school estate: Bitdefender documents backup-credential theft, rogue domain admins and new two-way trusts between Active Directory domains, with a command-retry pattern it reads as a model-driven loop

Bitdefender MDR attributes the intrusion to a 3AM (ThreeAM) ransomware affiliate on the encryptor build and its command-line pattern; the target was a school estate in the UK whose domains began as separate Active Directory environments, and initial access is unknown (Bitdefender, 2026-11-03). In September 2026 the attacker first took credentials from the backup software: a modified copy of a public script read the credentials stored in Veeam's databases on three backup servers and decrypted them with the Windows Data Protection API, and a browser credential database was copied from a terminal server (Bitdefender, 2026-11-03). It then worked with built-in tools (PowerShell, WMI, reg, netsh, rundll32) and a few public ones (an Impacket-like remote-execution tool that returns output over administrative shares, Mimikatz renamed to look like a monitoring binary), enumerated domain trusts from a domain controller, searched SYSVOL logon scripts for the names and subnets of other schools, created two backdoor domain-administrator accounts, joined three separate domains with two-way trusts within about three hours, tried to remove EDR agents, which anti-tampering controls blocked, deleted system-state backups and encrypted machines with a Rust-based encryptor (Bitdefender, 2026-11-03).

Bitdefender's reading, which it calls interpretation and not a finding, is that a model drove part of the work: commands call the Veeam web interface on a port and with a login method that do not match the vendor documentation, output is self-labelled, scripts carry numbered revisions, and retries arrive 40 to 101 seconds apart whatever the size of the change, while a new task takes minutes. Every attacker action Bitdefender saw came from an unmanaged internal host with no agent, so the automation itself was never seen, and Bitdefender says it could not document anything about a language model (Bitdefender, 2026-11-03).

Exposure
A Windows estate that runs Veeam Backup & Replication and has several Active Directory domains or a flat network that an unmanaged internal host can reach; the unmanaged host is the gap, because it ran no agent and sat outside Bitdefender's visibility.
Detection
In directory-service change events, new trust relationships between domains, which Bitdefender calls a rare change that is cheap to alert on, and new domain-administrator group members; in backup-server logs, Veeam web-interface calls and credential-store reads from hosts that are not backup administrators'; in endpoint telemetry, saves of the SECURITY, SYSTEM or SAM registry hives by any process that is not a known backup or administration job, LSASS access, a Windows Defender exclusion for the temporary directory, and the same command re-issued with small edits at a steady cadence; across hosts, file contents staged into registry values, which Bitdefender calls an unusual channel and a strong indicator to hunt for, and sent out by HTTP POST to an internal host, and probe or confirmation artifacts such as a scheduled task named for the probe left on production hosts; in authentication logs, unmanaged hosts authenticating to domain controllers (Bitdefender, 2026-11-03).
Defender takeaway
Alert on any new domain trust and on additions to the domain-administrator groups, alert on credential-reading access to backup-software databases and on saves of the SECURITY, SYSTEM or SAM hives outside known backup or administration jobs, put an endpoint agent on every machine because the staging host here was unmanaged, and limit remote execution and administrative shares to known management hosts (Bitdefender, 2026-11-03).

item.title: Binance's report: fake recruiter, trojaned pyenv, AI-tool pivot and a deployment token reached the signing service
item.description: Binance's report of 2026-11-03 says the theft of about USD 6.34 billion on 2026-10-29 was a multi-stage campaign: in September a software engineer contacted through a job platform was led through two fake interviews and told to download an assignment repository to his work computer, whose setup code replaced the pyenv executable in the Homebrew install with a malicious one that endpoint protection did not detect. On 2026-10-20 the attacker used that computer and an internal AI tool to take over two wallet-team engineers and found a container-deployment token, which on 2026-10-29 let it deploy a container and run a script that reached the wallet signing service. The FBI says North Korea was responsible and calls the activity TraderTraitor; Binance says some technical details stay confidential.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB2

Binance's own report on the 2026-10-29 theft of about USD 6.34 billion: a fake recruiter's coding assignment compromised an engineer's laptop, an internal AI tool carried the attacker to two colleagues and a container-deployment token, and a deployed container reached the wallet signing service; the FBI attributes it to North Korea's TraderTraitor

Binance says the theft of about USD 6.34 billion in digital assets on 2026-10-29 was "a sophisticated, multi-stage campaign" and not a single breach or a simple phishing incident (Binance, 2026-11-03). In September 2026 a software engineer whose job-platform profile named Binance was approached by a person posing as a project director, interviewed by a purported HR representative on live video and then by a purported CEO in a chat application, and told to download an "assignment" repository onto his work computer; its setup code replaced the legitimate pyenv executable in the Homebrew installation with a malicious version, repointed the symlink and spawned a zsh shell, and the 0-day malware was not detected by endpoint protection (Binance, 2026-11-03). On 2026-10-20 the attacker used that computer and an internal AI tool to gain control over a wallet DevOps engineer and a second wallet software engineer, and found a container-deployment permission token on the first engineer's computer; on 2026-10-29 it logged onto the second engineer's computer with the stolen credentials, deployed a container and triggered a script that launched the attack on the wallet signing service (Binance, 2026-11-03). Binance reports an earlier supply-chain event in June 2026, when a wallet DevOps engineer installed a tampered Homebrew installation while searching for an AI coding tool, and says its security team blocked 57 suspected North Korea-linked cases in 2026 (Binance, 2026-11-03). The FBI says North Korea was responsible and calls the activity "TraderTraitor" (FBI, 2026-10-31). BleepingComputer notes that fake job interviews leading to malware installs are a common tactic of the North Korean campaigns known as Contagious Interview and Operation Dream Job, a comparison Binance does not make (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-03).

The transfer to other organisations is the access chain, not the loss: a developer endpoint reached through a recruiting lure, a trojaned version-manager binary that endpoint protection missed, an internal AI tool that let one compromised user act on colleagues' machines, and a deployment token that turned one workstation into code execution in a trusted pipeline.

Exposure
Any organisation whose developers, DevOps or administrators can be approached through job platforms and run third-party assignment code on managed laptops, and any internal AI assistant or agent that can act with one employee's access on behalf of another.
Detection
In endpoint file-event telemetry, a version-manager or interpreter binary deleted, renamed and re-linked inside a package-manager directory followed by a shell spawned from it, which is the sequence Binance describes for pyenv in the Homebrew installation (Binance, 2026-11-03); in process lineage, shells started from a repository's setup scripts; in token-use logs, a container-deployment token used from a host that is not its owner's; in the access logs of internal AI tools, one user's session acting on other users' endpoints.
Defender takeaway
Treat a recruiter's "assignment" repository as untrusted code and keep it off managed machines, restrict what an internal AI tool can reach with one user's session and what a stored deployment token can deploy, and alert on shells spawned from replaced developer-tool binaries; Binance's own stated fixes are tighter device controls, rebuilt systems and tools, rotated credentials and tokens, and AI-based behavioural anomaly detection (Binance, 2026-11-03).

item.title: cPGuard update channel pushed a fake root update to about 2,950 servers on 2 Nov; update, then rotate root secrets
item.description: OPSSHIELD's disclosure of 2026-11-03 says an attacker registered as a customer on its billing portal and ran commands on the billing and licensing server, through crafted requests to the portal's callback pages (the vendor's logs do not record the exact request that gave access), took the keys used to publish updates and shipped a fake cPGuard update for about 70 minutes on 2026-11-02 (02:08 to 03:20 UTC). The update ran as root on about 2,950 customer servers, copied password hashes, root SSH keys, the MySQL root password and root shell history (cloud storage keys on a few) and left a hidden root shell and a scheduled task; about 7,900 billing-portal accounts were exposed as well. The clean update 5.88.26 removes the shell and a follow-up update removes the task, but credentials copied before cleanup may still be usable.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB2

OPSSHIELD cPGuard: an attacker who registered as a customer reached the vendor's billing and licensing server and shipped a fake update on 2026-11-02 that ran as root on about 2,950 Linux servers, copying root secrets and leaving a root shell and a scheduled task

OPSSHIELD says the attacker registered a customer account under a false identity on the vendor's billing portal, studied how the cPGuard agent talks to the licensing system with a trial install, sent crafted requests to the portal's callback pages, gained the ability to run commands on the billing and licensing server, took the keys used to publish updates and shipped a fake update for about 70 minutes on 2026-11-02; the vendor's logs do not record the exact request that gave access (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03). cPGuard agents installed the fake update between 02:08 and 03:20 UTC, and it ran as root (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03). The script copied the local password hashes, root's SSH private keys and authorization files, the MySQL root password and root's shell history back to the attacker, and root's cloud storage keys on a small number of servers; it also left a hidden root shell and a scheduled task (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03). The vendor puts the affected servers at about 2,950 and the exposed billing-portal accounts, with name, company, postal address, e-mail and hashed password, at about 7,900 (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03). A clean update, 5.88.26, removes the hidden root shell and a follow-up update removes the scheduled task (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03), but credentials copied before cleanup may still be usable (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03). The shared exposure is every operator of a cPGuard server: BleepingComputer says hosting firms and server administrators commonly run it alongside panels such as cPanel, DirectAdmin and Plesk (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-03).

Exposure
Any Linux server on which cPGuard was installed and online between 02:08 and 03:20 UTC on 2026-11-02; the vendor's earlier advisory framed the exposure as an install of versions 5.88.12 through 5.88.19 shown by "Successfully updated" entries in the product's install log, which proves installation and not that the script ran (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03), and the later disclosure narrows the fake update to 02:08 to 03:20 UTC without repeating a version range or withdrawing that check (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03). Holders of a billing-portal account are exposed separately.
Detection
In the install log, the affected version entries of 2026-11-02; on the host, the hidden root shell and the scheduled task the update left, which the vendor says to confirm are gone after updating; in authentication logs, root logins and use of the copied SSH keys from new sources after 2026-11-02, on this server and on every server that trusted its keys; in egress logs, the update script's collection and outbound copy of root's files.
Defender takeaway
Treat any server that ran the fake update as compromised for credential purposes even after the update: reset root and all local passwords, from a trusted environment as the earlier advisory says (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03), create new root SSH keys and remove the old public keys from every server that trusted them, change the MySQL root password and any database passwords it holds, rotate every secret in root's shell history and any cloud storage keys, and treat servers reached with those keys as exposed; rebuild from a clean backup taken before 1 November any server the vendor says the attacker logged in to by hand, and reset the billing-portal password with two-factor login (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03).

item.title: Barracuda ESG: no login needed, watchTowr shows one request reaches root; update to 9.4.0.029 or later
item.description: Barracuda's advisory of 2026-11-02 covers CVE-2026-116606, a pre-authentication authorization bypass in the Email Security Gateway (CVSS 9.3) that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker restore a crafted backup archive through the configuration-import function, and CVE-2026-111560, a command injection in the timezone field (8.6) that also affects the Load Balancer ADC, Message Archiver, WAF Control Center, Web Application Firewall and Web Security Gateway; chained, they give root. watchTowr Labs showed on 2026-11-05 that the chain needs no account, one unauthenticated request to the login handler reaching the restore function, and Barracuda changed its advisory the same day to say authentication is not required for CVE-2026-116606, only that the administrative interface must be reachable; watchTowr published a detection tool, and no source reports attacks. Barracuda names firmware 9.4.0.029 as the fixed build while the CVE record lists builds before 9.4.0.030 as affected.
item.content:encoded:
HIGHCVE-2026-116606 +1updatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-116606 / CVE-2026-111560, Barracuda Email Security Gateway: an unauthenticated configuration-import bypass chained with a root command injection, with watchTowr's full chain and a detection tool public since 2026-11-05; patches are out and no exploitation is reported (CVSS 9.3 and 8.6)

Barracuda's advisory of 2026-11-02 covers two flaws that, chained, give root on the appliance: CVE-2026-116606, a pre-authentication authorization bypass in the Email Security Gateway, and CVE-2026-111560, a command injection that also affects the Load Balancer ADC, Message Archiver, WAF Control Center, Web Application Firewall and Web Security Gateway (Barracuda, 2026-11-05). Barracuda says successful exploitation requires access to the administrative interface and that, in combination, the flaws let an attacker bypass authorization controls and obtain root (Barracuda, 2026-11-05). Mandiant's disclosure describes the first as letting an unauthenticated remote attacker invoke the gateway's configuration-import function and restore a crafted backup archive (Mandiant, 2026-11-02), and the second as shell metacharacters in the timezone configuration field that let an authenticated administrator run commands as root when the crafted value is processed (Mandiant, 2026-11-02). watchTowr Labs showed on 2026-11-05 that the two chain without any account on the gateway: one unauthenticated request reaches the restore function and the restored timezone value reaches the root command injection (watchTowr Labs, 2026-11-05). NCSC Switzerland rates the exploitation status unknown (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-11-03), and Barracuda changed its advisory on 2026-11-05 to say authentication is not required for CVE-2026-116606, only that the administrative user interface must be accessible to the attacker (Barracuda, 2026-11-05). No source reports attacks.

Barracuda released patches for each product and asks customers to apply any patch that was not applied automatically and to turn automatic patching on (Barracuda, 2026-11-05). Its Campus article names firmware 9.4.0.029 or later for the Email Security Gateway (Barracuda Campus, 2026-11-02), while the CVE record lists versions earlier than 9.4.0.030 as affected (Mandiant, 2026-11-02).

Exposure
An Email Security Gateway of any version before the fix, or a Load Balancer ADC, Message Archiver, WAF Control Center, Web Application Firewall or Web Security Gateway for the command injection, whose administrative interface can be reached; NCSC Switzerland puts internet-exposed management interfaces at the highest risk (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-11-03), and Barracuda says organisations whose administrative interfaces are not publicly accessible from the internet are less exposed to this attack path (Barracuda, 2026-11-05). The installed firmware version is shown under Advanced > Firmware Update (Barracuda Campus, 2026-11-02).
Detection
Barracuda's advisory names no indicators. watchTowr's chain implies, in the interface's web access logs, a POST to /cgi-mod/index.cgi that submits a password change with two different passwords together with a backup file from a session that never logged in, followed by a restored configuration whose timezone value holds shell metacharacters (watchTowr Labs, 2026-11-05); the mechanism also implies root-owned child processes under the appliance's management service after a restore nobody made.
Defender takeaway
Take the administrative interface of every affected Barracuda appliance off the internet and out of any untrusted network, update every Email Security Gateway to 9.4.0.029 or later, apply the patch listed for each of the other products and confirm that automatic patching is on; Barracuda recommends restricting administrative interfaces to trusted internal networks (Barracuda, 2026-11-05).
Update06 Nov 2026 03:41 UTCrun 2026-11-06T0255Z-inteltitleheadlinesummaryprioritytagscvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

watchTowr Labs published the full chain on 2026-11-05 after comparing firmware 9.4.0.027 with 9.4.0.029 (watchTowr Labs, 2026-11-05). In the login handler a failed password-change attempt returns the login-screen role instead of ending the request, so one unauthenticated POST to /cgi-mod/index.cgi that submits mismatching new and retyped passwords with a backup upload reaches the backup-restore function (watchTowr Labs, 2026-11-05). The restore accepts a backup whose checksum matches, and the checksum is built from the file bytes and a secret that is hard-coded in the product, so an attacker can build a valid archive (watchTowr Labs, 2026-11-05). A restored system_timezone value then reaches an unescaped shell call that runs as root (watchTowr Labs, 2026-11-05). watchTowr shares a Detection Artefact Generator so that owners can test their own appliances, and its post does not claim exploitation in the wild (watchTowr Labs, 2026-11-05). Its README describes a tool that takes a target URL and a command, builds a backup, uploads it to the target and attempts to check whether the target is vulnerable (watchTowr Labs README, 2026-11-03).

Barracuda changed its advisory the same day, 2026-11-05 at 2:30pm EST: the Authentication Required field for CVE-2026-116606 now reads No (Administrative UI Access Required), and the advisory says authentication is not required to exploit it but the administrative user interface must be accessible to the attacker (Barracuda, 2026-11-05). The advisory's entry for CVE-2026-111560 still reads Yes (Administrative Access) (Barracuda, 2026-11-05).

item.title: Update: Refrigeration attacks reach Switzerland, a Köniz butcher and three Volg stores; no actor established
item.description: The attacks reached Germany: heise reports an Edeka market in Reisbach whose cooling systems were heated to 50 degrees overnight into 2 November, WDR quotes a CAP supermarket manager saying the attack hit the firm that maintains the cooling plants remotely and reports that Rewe's head office confirmed an attack aimed at Danfoss; SentinelLABS says responsibility has not been publicly established; and Le Canard enchaîné reports that cold rooms of a contractor of the French blood service were programmed to 110 degrees overnight on 1 to 2 November, with no source tying that case to these controllers.
item.content:encoded:
Update04 Nov 2026 03:30 UTCrun 2026-11-04T0256Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarysourcesevidencesourcing_notebodyactions

The attacks reached Germany: heise reports an Edeka market in Reisbach whose cooling systems were heated to 50 degrees overnight into 2 November, WDR quotes a CAP supermarket manager saying the attack hit the firm that maintains the cooling plants remotely and reports that Rewe's head office confirmed an attack aimed at Danfoss; SentinelLABS says responsibility has not been publicly established; and Le Canard enchaîné reports that cold rooms of a contractor of the French blood service were programmed to 110 degrees overnight on 1 to 2 November, with no source tying that case to these controllers.

The first German cases followed on 2026-11-02: heise reports that the cooling systems of an Edeka market in Reisbach, Lower Bavaria, were heated to 50 degrees overnight into Monday and that the police have not confirmed a cyberattack as the cause, and WDR quotes a division manager at a CAP supermarket in North Rhine-Westphalia saying the actual attack hit the firm that maintains the cooling plants remotely, which is the operator's statement and not an authority finding, and Rewe's head office confirmed to WDR a cyberattack aimed specifically at the cooling-system supplier Danfoss, whose technology only a few regional Rewe stores use (translated from German) (heise, 2026-11-03; WDR, 2026-11-03). SentinelLABS' assessment of 2026-11-03 says responsibility for the European incidents has not been publicly established, calls Russian-aligned disruptive groups one credible hypothesis based on precedent, and says shared maintenance access deserves scrutiny (SentinelLABS, 2026-11-03). Le Canard enchaîné reports that Coolworld, a company that maintains refrigerated storage containers for the French blood service, was hacked overnight on 1 to 2 November and that cold rooms held at minus 30 degrees were programmed to reach 110 degrees; the blood service says an on-duty technician saw the temperature rise and acknowledges that frozen plasma intended for transfusion was among the products, and the Health Ministry says there was zero operational consequence because the situation was spotted (translated from French) (Le Canard enchaîné, 2026-11-03). The 110 degrees is the programmed set-point and not a measured temperature, and no source names the equipment, the vendor or the access method, or ties this case to the Danfoss and Copeland controllers.

Open finding: Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controllers compromised, with forced defrost at hundreds of French supermarkets, refrigeration failures at more than 115 shops in at least six more countries and first cases in Germany, and on 2026-11-02 altered settings in the cold rooms of the French blood service through a refrigeration supplier, and on 2026-11-05 the first publicly known cases in Switzerland; responsibility not established; ENISA and Europol call for immediate action →

item.title: Update: Refrigeration attacks reach Switzerland, a Köniz butcher and three Volg stores; no actor established
item.description: The attacks returned on 2026-11-02 across Belgium, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Sweden, Ireland and Estonia, and Finland per The Guardian: BleepingComputer counts more than 115 stores and says it is unclear whether the attacks were coordinated, Sabcobel says its sites were hit through the same vulnerability as in France, Euronews names Danfoss as the software supplier in both incidents while CyberInsider says the manufacturer and access method of the new wave remain unknown, and Coop Switzerland says attempts against it failed.
item.content:encoded:
Update03 Nov 2026 03:45 UTCrun 2026-11-03T0256Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarysourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

The attacks returned on 2026-11-02 across Belgium, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Sweden, Ireland and Estonia, and Finland per The Guardian: BleepingComputer counts more than 115 stores and says it is unclear whether the attacks were coordinated, Sabcobel says its sites were hit through the same vulnerability as in France, Euronews names Danfoss as the software supplier in both incidents while CyberInsider says the manufacturer and access method of the new wave remain unknown, and Coop Switzerland says attempts against it failed.

On 2026-11-02 refrigeration failures struck stores in Belgium, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Sweden, Ireland and Estonia, and Finland according to The Guardian; BleepingComputer counts more than 115 affected stores from company statements and says it is unclear whether they were hit in a coordinated attack, and several companies confirmed they had been hacked (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-02; The Guardian, 2026-11-02). Sabcobel's chief executive says the units' evaporators were switched to defrost mode (The Guardian, 2026-11-02) and, per BleepingComputer, that the attacker used the same vulnerability as in France (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-02); Euronews names Danfoss as the software supplier in both incidents and quotes it saying customers who had not updated their software were affected (Euronews, 2026-11-02), and in Estonia attackers reached the control computer of an older Danfoss system with outdated software (translated from German) (Tagesschau, 2026-11-02). CyberInsider nonetheless states that the manufacturer, controller models and initial access method of the new wave remain unknown (CyberInsider, 2026-11-02), so the vendor of the Belgian and Swedish sites is not independently confirmed. Coop Switzerland told 20 Minuten that corresponding attempts were registered without success, and Migros reports no indication of an attack (20 Minuten, 2026-11-02). The head of Sweden's national cybersecurity centre says it is working on incidents around the country and that Sweden has quite a lot of exposed operational technology devices (The Guardian, 2026-11-02).

Open finding: Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controllers compromised, with forced defrost at hundreds of French supermarkets, refrigeration failures at more than 115 shops in at least six more countries and first cases in Germany, and on 2026-11-02 altered settings in the cold rooms of the French blood service through a refrigeration supplier, and on 2026-11-05 the first publicly known cases in Switzerland; responsibility not established; ENISA and Europol call for immediate action →

item.title: Update: Node2Shell Brotli flaw is now on CISA KEV, with exploit traffic seen against Node.js 24.22.0; update now
item.description: Patchstack reports that default WordPress installs reach the Brotli decoder without authentication through the xmlrpc.php pingback and the operating system's libbrotli, shown to crash a worker but not to execute code; WordPress hosts need a patched libbrotli package, which the official WordPress image did not yet carry.
item.content:encoded:
Update03 Nov 2026 03:43 UTCrun 2026-11-03T0256Z-intelsourcesevidenceactionsbody

Patchstack reports that default WordPress installs reach the Brotli decoder without authentication through the xmlrpc.php pingback and the operating system's libbrotli, shown to crash a worker but not to execute code; WordPress hosts need a patched libbrotli package, which the official WordPress image did not yet carry.

Patchstack reports that WordPress ships no Brotli of its own but links the operating system's libbrotli through libcurl, so one unauthenticated POST to xmlrpc.php can take down a PHP worker on a stock install: the pingback method makes WordPress fetch an attacker-named URL and decode the Brotli reply (Patchstack, 2026-10-30). A laboratory demonstration killed a worker or pinned it at full CPU, its author says no code execution is included, and Patchstack says no public chain aims at PHP; the fix is a patched libbrotli package, and the official wordpress:latest image still carried a vulnerable one when Patchstack wrote (Patchstack, 2026-10-30).

Open finding: CVE-2026-111497, Node.js and Google Brotli (Node2Shell): an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder lets crafted compressed data run code, reached through fetch() and Express 5 or body-parser 2 request bodies; fixed in Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 and in the PyPI packages Brotli 1.2.1 and brotlicffi 1.2.1.0 (CVSS 4.0 9.2) →

item.content:encoded:
Update03 Nov 2026 03:41 UTCrun 2026-11-03T0256Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarycvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

CloudLinux's kernel team could not reproduce Anthropic's remote-root exploit, Fortinet lists FortiOS, FortiProxy, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiWeb and FortiAuthenticator among the products under investigation with no fixed build, AWS publishes per-service fix status and Akamai reports a similar flaw reached through request-socket migration; Amazon Linux and CIQ's RLC Pro 8, 9 and 10 kernels are now fixed.

Fortinet published advisory FG-IR-26-188 on 2026-11-02, saying it is investigating the impact on its products and listing FortiOS, FortiProxy, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiWeb and FortiAuthenticator among them, with no fixed build or workaround named (Fortinet, 2026-11-02). CloudLinux's kernel team could not reproduce Anthropic's remote-root claim (CloudLinux, 2026-11-02). AWS says fixed Amazon Linux 2 and 2023 kernels are available, that Network Load Balancer TCP listeners pass client packets, including IP options, to targets, and that Linux targets behind them, Global Accelerator, PrivateLink and VPC Lattice layer 4 need the kernel update or the interim steps themselves, in the bulletin as published on 2026-11-02; its revision of 2026-11-04 says Global Accelerator endpoints are not affected and no longer carries the Network Load Balancer paragraph (AWS, 2026-11-02). Akamai reports a similar flaw when request-socket migration is enabled and lists the stable fixes 5.10.272, 5.15.223, 6.1.190, 6.6.159, 6.12.113, 6.18.56 and 7.2.10 (Akamai, 2026-11-02). CIQ's table lists patched kernels for RLC Pro 8, 9 and 10 and FIPS 8.6 and 8.10 released on 2026-11-01 (CIQ, 2026-11-01).

Open finding: CVE-2026-98432, Linux kernel IPv4 TCP: a use-after-free in connection setup, present since 4.4, has an Anthropic-built remote root exploit against MPTCP listeners that CloudLinux could not reproduce; Citrix XenServer, XCP-ng, MikroTik, Red Hat, Debian, CIQ and Amazon Linux have fixes, Ubuntu's are in progress and WatchGuard and Fortinet have none for their products (CVSS 9.8) →

item.content:encoded:
Improvement03 Nov 2026 03:32 UTCrun 2026-11-03T0256Z-intelheadlinesummarycvestechniquessourcesevidencesourcing_notebody

Progress's bulletin carries fifteen WS_FTP Server flaws, six of them critical; CVE-2026-90868, CVE-2026-90866, CVE-2026-90864 and CVE-2026-90863 need privileges, and NCSC Switzerland describes four of the critical flaws as a route from the exposed administrator credentials to full server compromise.

Six of the bulletin's fifteen flaws are critical: besides CVE-2026-84295 and CVE-2026-90865, CVE-2026-90868 (9.9), CVE-2026-90866, CVE-2026-90864 and CVE-2026-90863 (9.1 each), and NCSC Switzerland ties the credential exposure in CVE-2026-84295 to command injection and scope-escape flaws that lead to a complete compromise of the server (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-11-02; heise online, 2026-11-02). All four added flaws need privileges: CVE-2026-90866 (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-29), CVE-2026-90864 (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-29) and CVE-2026-90863 (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-29) need a delegated Host Administrator, and CVE-2026-90868 (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-29) is scored for an attacker with low privileges.

Open finding: CVE-2026-84295, Progress WS_FTP Server: an unauthenticated remote authentication flaw can expose administrative credentials (CVSS 10.0), with two more unauthenticated flaws, fixed in 2025.0.4 and 2024.0.7; no exploitation found →
